I looked into why this PR still reads `BLOCKED` after three weeks, and the reason is mechanical rather than a missing approval.

The required `test` and `typecheck` workflows on this branch are stuck in `action_required` — they were never approved, so they never ran:

- `test` → run 32837016989 (2026-08-25, `action_required`)
- `typecheck` → run 32837016988 (2026-08-25, `action_required`)
- `pr-standards` → run 32837014356 (`success`; `pull_request_target`, so it runs without approval)

`gh pr checks` only lists the two checks that actually executed, which is why the PR looks like it is blocked on review when the real gap is the unapproved first-time-contributor run.

I cannot clear it from my side: I have `push: false` on the upstream repository, and a fork author cannot approve their own workflow run. A maintainer clicking **Approve and run** on the `test` and `typecheck` runs (or re-running them) will let both checks report.

Status of the change itself: still conflict-free against `v2` (`mergeable: MERGEABLE`, `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`), and the unit + typecheck suites only ever ran locally, not in CI. The same pattern applies to my other PR #43282.

### Second confirmation: macOS + OpenChamber, opencode serve 1.18.30 (homebrew)

Same accumulation on a different platform and client series. This is the per-request/per-connection instance path (#47727) and should be tracked separately from the browser-reconnect path (#46035), as requested.

**Environment**
- macOS (Apple Silicon), node v24.19.0 (nvm)
- opencode **1.18.30** (homebrew), launched by OpenChamber desktop as `opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 50905`
- Global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`) has exactly **2 local stdio MCP servers** (`openspec` via `npx -y openspec-mcp`, `gitnexus` via `gitnexus mcp`) plus one remote

**Live census** (single serve PID, uptime ~4 min, idle, only one active chat)
- serve holds **21 complete MCP sets**, every process a direct child of serve (PPID = serve), **zero orphans** (no PPID 1), all launchers alive, one set per connection:
  - 21 × `npm exec openspec-mcp` (wrapper, 41–65 MB) → 21 × `node …/openspec-mcp` (30–54 MB)
  - 21 × `gitnexus mcp` (node, 47–69 MB)
- Total = 63 MCP child processes ≈ **4 GB**, plus the serve process itself at **~940 MB** → ~5 GB from 50+ node processes minutes after launching the client.
- Spawns arrived in 3 bursts (28 @ 09:53:16, 20 @ 09:53:48, 6 @ 09:55:14): one round at startup warming sets, then further rounds per connection — matching an instance materialized per connection/request and never disposed.
- Network: OpenChamber holds ~12 ESTABLISHED TCP connections to `:50905`; serve also keeps ~20 loopback connections to its own port (same self-loopback shape reported in #46035). Every MCP child keeps a live PIPE to serve — active processes, not zombies.

This reproduces #47727 on stable 1.18.30 with a desktop/web client that polls directories (OpenChamber), on macOS, with no TUI client attached — sets keyed per (connection/directory instance), never reused, never reaped. Happy to attach full `ps` trees or `lsof` dumps if useful.

Confirmed on macOS with OpenCode **1.18.30**. This also affects CLI/TUI startup: running `opencode` fails with “Unexpected server error,” and the server log reports `SQLiteError: no such column: project_id` in `Project.migrateProjectId`.

The database’s `workspace` columns are `id`, `provider`, `binding`, `created_at`, and `last_used_at`. The repository’s `.git/opencode` cache contained an older project ID, while all ten existing v2 sessions for the directory already referenced the current remote-derived project ID.

After backing up and correcting only the cached project ID, startup succeeded without manually changing the database schema or session rows. Both `opencode` and its shell alias were then verified in tmux 3.6a: the home screen loaded, the command palette responded, and both exited with status 0.

This is a workaround for this particular state; the incompatible migration remains in 1.18.30.

Full evidence bundle (ps trees, complete lsof dumps, network/set census) captured live on stable 1.18.30 / macOS / OpenChamber:

**Evidence bundle**: https://gist.github.com/sugarless-sweet/588effc909b71faa6d3e46c52a4e2c81

Highlights:
- In this brand-new session the serve process already re-materialized MCP sets and RSS reached **~1.46 GB within ~12 min**.
- **2 complete sets** = 6 direct children (npm exec openspec → node openspec, gitnexus), zero orphans, all launchers alive. The 2nd set appeared *later* (etime 13:31 vs 13:48) → per-connection/request materialization.
- Caught a **transient extra `node openspec-mcp` spawn (2 MB) mid-census** — accumulation was actively ongoing during sampling, not a one-time warm-up.
- Network: serve holds 5 loopback self-conns to its own port; OpenChamber holds 5 conns → **set count ≠ connection count**, consistent with one set per directory/request instance never disposed (#47727).
- Earlier session (serve 35235, since shut down) had accumulated **21 sets / 63 children / ~4 GB** within minutes, plus serve at ~940 MB.

Full ready-to-attach reproduction data in the bundle; happy to add periodic samplings to show the growth curve if it helps.

Confirmed on a live NixOS host today: the managed `serve` (pid ~1.5k-task agent scope, `memory.high` stalling, `TasksMax` pressure) was repeatedly probed past 2s and recycled — exactly this loop.

Draft fix in #48591: on Linux, when a user session bus and `systemd-run` exist, `Daemon.start()` spawns via `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect`, so the serve lands in its own transient scope — a sibling of the client's cgroup. Verified end-to-end: serve pid landed in `app.slice/run-p<id>.scope` next to (not inside) the client's scope; `service status`/`stop` still work and the scope is collected on exit. Fallback path is unchanged on other platforms.

Addendum with the decisive evidence — I found the exact ruleset rule this collides with.

`GET /repos/anomalyco/opencode/rules/branches/v2` (ruleset 19434226, active) requires precisely these five contexts:

```
unit (linux), unit (windows), e2e (linux), e2e (windows), typecheck
```

All five are produced by the **`test` workflow** (`.github/workflows/test.yml`), which runs on `pull_request` and therefore waits for approval on first-time-contributor PRs. My runs are still unapproved:

- `test` → run 32837016989 — `action_required`
- `typecheck` → run 32837016988 — `action_required`

So **every single required check is one of the checks that never ran.** The only checks that did report (`check-compliance`, `check-standards`, from `pull_request_target`-based `pr-standards`) are not in the required list at all — which is why the PR reads `BLOCKED` while `gh pr checks` shows green.

For contrast, #48249 (a fork PR by @Tarquinen, merged 2026-09-10) had its runs approved, so all five required contexts reported and it merged:

```
test      | completed/failure  <- ran, so the checks reported
typecheck | completed/success
unit (linux) pass · unit (windows) fail · e2e (linux) pass · e2e (windows) pass · typecheck pass
```

Note that its `unit (windows)` result was a **failure** and it still merged — so this is not a "must be green" bar, it is purely that the checks have to be *reported*.

The v2 ruleset also sets `required_approving_review_count: 0`, so no review is needed to unlock this — only **Approve and run** on the `test` and `typecheck` runs for this branch (and the same for #43282). I have `push: false` on the repo so I cannot trigger or approve them myself.

Additional impact observed in OpenCode 1.18.30: strict closed single-select prompts require both `multiple: false` and `custom: false` to be exposed and honored by the tool schema/runtime.

`multiple` is already available, but because `custom` is absent from `Question.Prompt`, callers cannot disable free-text answers. Safety-sensitive consumers therefore cannot represent a closed answer domain in the native question UI and must fall back or stop.

#45236 appears to address the missing field. This note is only to record the closed-domain use case; I did not open a separate issue for it.

Same root cause here — confirmed by measurement: `Command.init` awaits `mcp.prompts()`, and the MCP `InstanceState` init blocks until every enabled server settles (30s timeout each), so `GET /command` doesn't return until then. With a slow-but-eventually-connecting server you get a multi-second delay (5.6s measured with 9 servers); with a server whose handshake never completes, the palette stays empty until timeout — which matches what you're seeing.

I've opened #48630, which makes `/command` return file-based commands immediately and merge MCP prompts asynchronously via a `command.updated` event.
